lessons.goal: 從行動順序推論目標拆分如何影響人物行為。

questions.evidence: Sam keeps writing 'Improve my English' at the top of his weekend list. The phrase feels important, but when Saturday arrives he cannot decide where to begin. He opens several books, changes his mind, and spends more time choosing than reading.
questions.explanation: 大目標太籠統，使他忙於選材料而未開始。
options: He cannot find any books.
He has no interest in improving.
He cannot identify a starting action.
He has already completed every skill.
questions.prompt: What difficulty does Sam have with his original goal?

questions.evidence: This week, he writes a smaller action: read one short passage and explain why one tempting wrong option is wrong. He puts the passage and a pencil on his desk the night before. The task has a visible starting point and a clear ending.
questions.explanation: 新目標是短文加一題誘答錯因解釋。
options: Memorize all possible answers.
Read a short passage and explain one tempting wrong option.
Finish every English book on Saturday.
Predict an official exam level.
questions.prompt: What specific task does he set?

options: To make starting the chosen task easier.
To prove the answer is correct.
To remove the need for an ending.
To stop all later reading.
questions.prompt: Why put the passage and pencil out the night before?

options: Attractive enough to seem worth choosing.

options: It replaces every other skill forever.
It guarantees complete mastery of English.
It makes a broad goal repeatable through a defined action.
It ensures Sam always reads two passages.
questions.prompt: What does the smaller task accomplish without claiming too much?
